LMP3.title: United’s #3 Ligier wins at Silverstone as Eurointernational’s pole fades
LMP3.dek: Wells, Grist and Bell won for United Autosports by about nine seconds over Ecurie Ecosse’s Ligier, the team’s first win of 2018, while pole-sitting Eurointernational finished tenth in class.

facts.v: Drudi’s 1:55.508 gave Eurointernational its first pole, four hundredths clear of Kaiser’s 360 Racing Ligier.

one.label: Sportscar365: Stevens Beats Vergne to 4H Silverstone Pole

facts.v: The #3 gave United its first LMP3 victory of the season and its first since the Algarve the year before.

chapters.title: Eighteen Ligiers and Normas on a new surface
text: Eighteen LMP3 cars lined up for the 4 Hours of Silverstone, with RLR MSport’s #15 arriving as the class points leader. The entry list had been reshuffled in the days before the race. DKR Engineering stayed away, and Henning Enqvist, who had driven its Norma in Austria, joined Team Virage instead. Virage, which had appeared at Monza only under the Racing For Poland banner, ran under its own name for the first time, with Littman making his LMP3 debut.
Yann Clairay replaced Mikkel Jensen in AT Racing’s #9, and Cool Racing’s #4 had Lucas Borga in for one race in place of his brother Antonin, who was due back at Spa.

Silverstone had been resurfaced earlier in the year, and the darker tarmac held heat and left short bumps at Maggotts and Stowe that unsettled cars under braking. United took the first two places in opening practice, Bell’s 1:55.689 the best in class, with seven Ligiers in the top seven. In the second session Kaiser put the #6 360 Racing Ligier on top in the closing minutes, three tenths clear of the #2 United car.

chapters.title: Drudi takes Eurointernational’s first pole
text: The session finished like a fruit machine. Bell had briefly led for United, but Drudi answered late to put the Eurointernational Ligier #12 on pole with a 1:55.508, only 0.046 seconds ahead of Kaiser in the #6 360 Racing car. It was the first pole for both the driver and the team, and Drudi said he liked the track and hoped to race the same way.

A late exchange with Rayhall left Ligiers locking out the first two rows: Rayhall’s #2 was third on 1:55.662, with Bell’s #3 fourth on 1:55.803. Lahaye took the honours among the Normas in Ultimate’s #17, fifth on 1:56.079, ahead of the points leader, van Uitert in RLR’s #15, on 1:56.195. Kapadia’s Ecurie Ecosse Ligier #7 was seventh.

chapters.title: United’s second car drops back, Grist moves up
text: Drudi led away from pole, but the front row did not stay intact. Rayhall’s #2 and Kaiser’s #6 both had incidents in the opening turns and were left at the back of the field. That lifted Grist into second in the #3 United Ligier from fourth on the grid, and he was within half a second of Drudi in traffic. Rayhall then drove a strong recovery, up to eighth by lap 15 and fifth ten laps later. The first round of stops came under a full-course yellow with the order unchanged, and the only driver change in the leading group was Bell taking over the second-placed #3.

chapters.title: Bell passes Drudi and the lead holds
text: With the green flag back, Bell was all over Drudi and made the decisive move around the outside at Luffield, then eased out a lead of more than ten seconds that was rarely threatened. Rayhall went past van Uitert’s RLR car for second and the #2 was soon handed to Falb, giving United a one-two after two rounds of stops, with Wells in the lead car. Kapadia climbed to third for Ecurie Ecosse and Farano fought back to fourth at the end of the third hour.

Drudi’s #12 faded once Dromedari took the wheel, which pushed the #6 up the order, and Ultimate’s #17 was the best-placed Norma in fifth. The last stops reshaped the order again. A slow final stop for the #2 dropped it down to seventh in class, which promoted Noble’s #7 to second with 45 minutes left. The #6 lost third place at Luffield, Lahaye moved the #17 up to third, and Swift recovered the Ligier to fourth.

chapters.title: Wells wins for United by nine seconds
text: Noble closed in during the final stint but could reduce the gap only to about nine seconds, and Wells took the flag for the #3 Ligier to give Wells, Grist and Bell the win. It was the first success for the crew and the team’s first LMP3 win since the Algarve the previous year. “I’m ecstatic to win this race!” Wells said afterwards, praising a faultless team and pit stops, and adding that he never went well at Silverstone.

chapters.title: United’s breakthrough and Eurointernational’s tenth
text: The #3 won on 117 laps for Wells, Grist and Bell. Noble, Kapadia and Stubbe Olsen took second for Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen on the same lap, with the Lahaye family and Heriau third in Ultimate’s Norma #17 and the #6 of Woodward, Kaiser and Swift fourth, both also on 117. Inter Europol’s #13 was fifth on 116, RLR’s #15 sixth and United’s #2 seventh, both a lap down, followed by M. Racing-YMR’s Norma #19.

Pole-sitting Eurointernational’s #12 finished tenth in class on 116 laps, though Drudi set the class fastest lap, 1:57.769. Of the 18 starters, 16 were classified; NEFIS’s #5 (84 laps) and M. Racing-YMR’s Ligier #18 (61) were not. The ELMS next went to Spa on 23 September.

LMGTE.title: JMW survives a ten-second penalty to beat Proton at Silverstone
LMGTE.dek: Liam Griffin, MacDowall and Molina won for JMW’s Ferrari after Molina passed Matt Griffin late and finished just over ten seconds clear of Proton’s #88 Porsche, absorbing a track-limits penalty.

facts.t: Proton lock out the front row

facts.v: Ebimotors’ #80 and Gulf’s #86 both made their race debuts at Silverstone, Ebimotors having borrowed a Proton car in the opening rounds.
JMW’s Ferrari and Spirit of Race’s #55 both received 10-second penalties for repeated track-limits abuse; Molina’s advantage at the flag was just over that.

chapters.title: Seven cars, two new Porsches and a double duty weekend
text: Seven LMGTE cars started at Silverstone, and two of them were Porsche 911 RSRs that had not raced before. Ebimotors’ #80 was a brand new car, which freed the Proton chassis it had borrowed in the opening rounds to return to WEC duty, and Gulf Racing UK’s #86 was making its first start, the last of the 2017 batch of customer cars.

The round shared Silverstone with the WEC’s six-hour race the following day, so several crews were stretched across two paddocks. Gulf’s Barker, Davison and Wainwright drove both cars, with Barker saying the WEC was the priority and that the ELMS run was mainly to give Bronze-rated Wainwright more track time, as the team was not in the ELMS championship. Matt Griffin was in his sixth consecutive year of doing both races, and Proton also ran in both. The #88 Proton Porsche led the class standings, with Ebimotors in contention with it.

In first practice Barker’s #86 was fastest on 2:00.345, with the #77 a tenth behind and the #88, the points leader, fifth after a transmission problem late in the session. That was repaired before the second session, when Cairoli set the class best of 1:59.474, two tenths clear of Matt Griffin’s #55 Spirit of Race Ferrari.

chapters.title: Olsen gives Proton the front row
text: Olsen took pole for Proton Competition’s #77 Porsche with a 1:58.704, 0.060 seconds ahead of Cairoli in the sister #88, completing a one-two for the German team. It was Proton’s second ELMS pole of the season. Olsen said he almost spun at the chicane on his lap, and that an overnight set-up change had helped.

Barker’s #86 Gulf Porsche was third on 1:58.845, less than two tenths off the pole. Molina took the #66 JMW Ferrari fourth on 1:58.972 and Matt Griffin was fifth in the #55 Spirit of Race car on 1:59.141, though both had quicker laps deleted for track limits. Pera’s Ebimotors #80 was sixth on 1:59.378, ahead of Bertolini in Krohn Racing’s #83 Ferrari on 1:59.521.

chapters.title: Roda jumps the pole-sitter
text: Gianluca Roda took the Proton #88 past pole-sitter Ried at the start, reversing the Porsche front row. Behind them the Ferraris of Liam Griffin and Cameron traded paint at The Loop, Griffin having to defend hard in the #66 before the Spirit of Race car took third. Cameron was soon in the wars again at Luffield, where a lapping LMP2 car made contact, and he then pushed Ried onto the dirt at Aintree in a move for second.

chapters.title: The lead changes through the pit stops
text: After the first stops the #88 was back in front and Aaron Scott ran second in the #55, with MacDowall third in the #66. The second round of stops changed the lead: the #88 spent longer in the pits, which handed the front to the Spirit of Race Ferrari, with MacDowall all over it until the #66 pitted. Cameron took the lead back a lap after rejoining just behind the JMW car.

Proton’s two Porsches ran third and fourth, and Roda made a bold move around the outside of Liam Griffin at Stowe to close on the leader. Griffin took the place back before pitting, leaving Molina second ahead of Cairoli with Matt Griffin now in the Spirit of Race car. The stewards were by then watching track limits, and JMW’s Ferrari was shown a 10-second penalty.

chapters.title: Molina catches Griffin, then the stopwatch
text: Molina closed on Matt Griffin until the gap was under three seconds, then passed him into Luffield. Spirit of Race had its own 10-second penalty for track limits, to be added at the end, as neither car had another stop to take it in. Cairoli was third and penalty-free, only 7.4 seconds behind the pair, so the race looked set for the Porsche.

Griffin’s tyres were fading and he had a wide moment on the last lap, while Cairoli also ran wide at the final corner. Molina took the flag just over ten seconds clear of Cairoli, enough to cover the penalty. He said the team had all driven well, that he did not know how he recovered everything and that he still could not believe it.

chapters.title: JMW’s second win of the year
text: The #66 won on 115 laps for Liam Griffin, MacDowall and Molina, JMW’s second win of the season. Proton’s #88 (Gianluca Roda, Giorgio Roda Jr and Cairoli) was second, Spirit of Race’s #55 third and Proton’s #77 fourth, all on the same lap. Matt Griffin was comfortably clear of the fourth-placed Porsche.

Gulf’s #86 was fifth on its race debut, a lap down on 114, and Krohn’s #83 sixth on 112. Ebimotors’ new #80 completed 112 laps but was not classified. Cairoli set the class fastest lap, 2:00.290. The ELMS next went to Spa on 23 September.
